note.text:
Air is a mixture, not a compound. Evidence:
• Its composition varies from place to place (more water vapour near the sea, more carbon dioxide in a crowded room).
• Its gases can be separated by physical methods (fractional distillation of liquid air).
• Each gas keeps its own properties (oxygen in air still supports burning).
• Air can be made by mixing the gases with no heat change and no reaction.
• Air has no fixed formula, and liquid air has no single boiling point.
A compound, by contrast, has a fixed composition and a formula, and can only be separated by a chemical reaction.

vars.x: liquid air boils over a range of temperatures

steps: A pure substance (an element or compound) has one fixed boiling point.
A mixture boils over a range because its parts boil at different temperatures.

cards.idea: Air is a mixture because its composition varies and it has no formula.
example: Air in a crowded room has more carbon dioxide.
Air near the sea has more water vapour.

cards.idea: The gases in air keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods.
example: Oxygen in air still relights a glowing splint slowly.

pick.q: Air can be made by mixing nitrogen and oxygen. What is observed?
pick.r: No heat change and no new substance
pick.y: Mixing gases is a physical process.

pick.q: How are the gases of air separated?
pick.r: by fractional distillation of liquid air
e: Air is a mixture, so physical methods work.
pick.y: A physical method separates a mixture.

cards.idea: A compound has a fixed composition and a formula; it is separated only by a chemical reaction.

pick.q: Is air an element, a compound or a mixture?
e: A compound has a fixed formula; air has none.
pick.y: Air is a mixture of gases.

pick.q: Which observation shows that air is a mixture?
pick.r: Its composition varies from place to place.
pick.y: A compound always has the same composition.

pick.q: Which of these is a compound?
e: Air is a mixture of gases.
Sea water is salt mixed with water.
pick.y: Water has a fixed formula, H₂O.

pick.q: Which is true of a compound but not of air?
pick.r: It has a fixed composition and a formula.
pick.y: Air has no formula; its composition varies.

pick.q: Air can be made by mixing nitrogen and oxygen. What is observed?
pick.r: No heat change and no new substance
pick.y: Mixing gases is a physical process.

pick.q: How are the gases of air separated?
pick.r: by fractional distillation of liquid air
e: Air is a mixture, so physical methods work.
pick.y: A physical method separates a mixture.

right.text: The parts of air can be separated physically.
Water is a compound with a fixed composition.
Oxygen in air keeps its own properties.

wrong.text: Air is a compound because it always has the same composition.
wrong.explain: Air's composition varies; it is a mixture.

wrong.text: Liquid air boils at one fixed temperature.
wrong.explain: It boils over a range: it is a mixture.

wrong.text: Air can only be separated by a chemical reaction.
wrong.explain: Air is separated by fractional distillation, a physical method.
